Take this free CAT Linear Equations online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Linear Equations chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Linear Equations tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Linear Equations

Solving linear equations and systems, conditions for unique / infinite / no solution, and word problems with integer constraints.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Unique solution if a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂.
  • Infinite solutions if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.
  • No solution if a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂.
  • Translate each sentence into one equation; count unknowns.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Confusing the infinite-solution and no-solution conditions.
  • Ignoring integer/positivity constraints in word problems.
  • Arithmetic slips in elimination.

Ten honest questions teach more than fifty solved passively.
